scene.note: Before anything changes, the report is timed step by step and its work is counted.

steps.note: The match step is handed over to be timed. Its first run happens once and is not kept.
Then it runs several times, each one timed from just before to just after, waiting for it to finish.
The times are sorted, and the one in the middle is what a usual run takes.
The report has three steps of work: match, money and print. Each one is timed on its own.
One step is timed after the other, never two at once, so no time takes in another's.
Idris gets a list with the slowest step first.
A function the report calls again and again, like the comparison of a sort, is wrapped.
The wrapped function does exactly what it did before, and adds one to its count each time it runs.
The count is the same on every computer, so it says how much work the report does, not how fast this machine is.
